result.answer: That is already how this site is set up. The bed-management system behind Downstream Out keeps only the patient's current placement. It shows the patient on WARD-C, bay BAY1-07, from a later transfer (event time 09:45 UTC). It has no receipt for the failed transfer to WARD-B (09:20 UTC), which failed because the system was unavailable. With only the current placement needed, the WARD-B transfer adds nothing. Resending it would move the patient back to a ward they have already left. So Shutter closed the case and sent nothing, and nothing needs to change. The only thing lost is the record of the WARD-B stop. Under the full-history alternative, the case would have gone to a person instead (W1). The members agree on the outcome but stress different things. The encounter member says Shutter cannot tell whether anyone downstream needs the WARD-B stay. The impact member says the bed board, pharmacy and porters are already correct, and a resend would mislead them. The conformance member says the message itself was fine, but only its structure was checked. No site-rule review is on record.

perspectives.view: The WARD-B placement was overtaken by the applied WARD-C transfer, so it adds nothing when only the current placement matters. Shutter cannot tell whether anyone needs the WARD-B stay.

The systems that read the bed-management system already see WARD-C. Resending would show the wrong bed and could misdirect pharmacy and porters. What the full-history correction would trigger downstream is unknown.

The message parsed cleanly as version 2.5.1 and was not the cause of the failure (HTTP 503). Only its structure was checked, so a site-rule problem cannot be ruled out. Either way, it is not worth resending.

setting.why: This receiver keeps only the current state, which is why the overtaken transfer was closed with nothing sent.
